I pick arguments or create drama to distract myself from the trauma
Making any plans for the future

Threat.value: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Memory.value: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
There are parts of the event that I simply cannot remember no matter how hard I try
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.

issues.item: Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
issues.explanation: 'Irritability' is not a threat appraisal/perception item; it reflects arousal/behavioral dysregulation and fits better outside the Threat node. In this profile, the other Threat items are coherent terrorism-related hypervigilance/safety behaviors ('Scanning Exits', 'Back to Wall'), so this item is internally mismatched within the node and weakly aligned with the formulation in which Memory-linked threat should reflect perceived current danger rather than aggressive behavior.

vignette: Kofi is a 33-year-old African man who works as a tailor in his community. He has been single for several years and spends most of his time focusing on his craft. On the surface, Kofi appears to be a dedicated worker, but beneath this veneer lies a complex web of trauma symptoms that have significantly impacted his life. Kofi was a victim of a terrorist attack at a local market he frequented regularly. The event left him in a state of shock and fear. He vividly recalls the chaos and panic as the attackers roamed freely through the crowd, but these memories often come with feelings of numbness, as if he were observing someone else's trauma. This sense of detachment has made it challenging for Kofi to fully process what happened. At times, entire segments of that day are shrouded in a fog of memory gaps, leaving him frustrated and anxious about the unknown details. Since the attack, Kofi has developed an intense need for control and safety, which manifests in his hypervigilant behavior. He now scans for exits as soon as he enters any room or building and feels safest when his back is against a wall where he can see everything happening around him. This constant state of alertness has become a significant part of his daily routine. The traumatic event has also deeply affected Kofi's self-perception. He harbors doubts about his ability to make the right decisions, feeling weak and unable to trust himself. These negative appraisals have led him to seek escape through maladaptive strategies. For instance, he spends long hours on his phone playing games or browsing the internet as a way to avoid thinking about what happened. This habit has gradually increased over time, leaving him isolated from others. Kofi's tendency to pick arguments and create drama is another coping mechanism that emerged after the trauma. He finds that these conflicts distract him from the lingering fears and memories of the attack. However, this behavior has strained his relationships with colleagues and friends, further isolating him. The memory replay he experiences serves as a constant reminder of the event. These intrusive recollections often play out like a film in his mind, overwhelming him and driving him back to his maladaptive strategies for relief. The more Kofi tries to avoid these memories by engaging in distractions or conflicts, the stronger they become, creating a vicious cycle that leaves him feeling increasingly trapped. Kofi's hypervigilance has also led him to develop additional avoidance behaviors, such as avoiding making any future plans. This fear of unpredictability and potential danger keeps him from committing to anything beyond his immediate surroundings. The more he avoids these situations, the deeper his sense of self-doubt grows, reinforcing the belief that he is weak and unable to cope. What frightens Kofi most is the possibility of another attack and the realization that he might not be able to protect himself or others. He finds himself constantly scanning for threats and feeling unsafe in public spaces, which has led him to work longer hours at his tailor shop to avoid going out. This pattern of behavior has taken a toll on both his personal life and professional relationships. Kofi's current state is one of deep distress and uncertainty. The combination of hypervigilance, memory intrusions, negative self-perceptions, and maladaptive coping strategies has created a cycle that he feels unable to break free from on his own. He finally decided to seek help when the isolation and constant fear began affecting his ability to work effectively and maintain any meaningful connections with others. Kofi hopes for support in understanding and managing these overwhelming symptoms so that he can regain control of his life and reconnect with the world around him.
